question: Which post-source-Close operations require real namespace operands or allocation capacity, and which alleged bounds remain unproved?
method: Read-only immutable git show and pinned Go1.26.4 source inspection; no edits, builds, tests, benchmarks or new ownership authority.
findings: Replacement idx and source DB close before cache invalidation, COMMIT create/write/fsync/barriers, full pair verification, serial DATA/PRIMARY rename/reopen validation, final pair verification and decision removal.

Original proof/resource construction occurs before these closes. The core post-close chain does not directly construct a new Owner, registry or proof; hidden validation opens still need pre-admission.

Cache invalidation and failed staging cleanup have two transient child Files besides parent. COMMIT uses one transient child. Pair verification/renames have at most two transient children besides parent and are serial.
COMMIT encoding permits payload <=4096/image <=4140, but json.Marshal allocates before the length check. Pre-close sizing/preborn scratch is still an implementation obligation.

Two capsule candidates each with current/embedded-parent frontier do not bound original DATA verification memory: ReadPage page images, reservation metadata, visited map and recursive nodes scale with real generation contents.
Legacy quarantine recovery nominally peaks at six real handles with synchronous successful closes, plus retained expected parent. The selected File factor must account for its exact genuine overlaps.
ReadDir(2) is not a complete 0/1/>1 census on a short nil-error return: n decrements before ENOENT entries are skipped. Loop until two returned entries or genuine EOF.

First directory read creates dirInfo and may allocate an 8192-byte pooled buffer plus slice header. Returned entries allocate names, unixDirent and result-slice backing; eager/unknown-type fstatat allocates fileStat. StableFileMetadataCharge alone excludes these families.
Root-opened Files eagerly stat every entry; os.NewFile may trust known d_type. Selected factoring must deliberately preserve fail-closed identity/type/error behavior using admitted original operands.

Directory parser checks each record against current 8192-byte buffer and each name slice against its record. This permits a pinned-runtime conservative per-name byte ceiling, not a filesystem NameMax assertion.

Go atomic.Pointer[T] includes zero-length [0]*T type field, allowing reflection on type metadata to reach os.dirInfo representation without reading live pointers or constructing directories. Concrete supported layout/provenance checks remain implementation obligations.
Old-segment health updates/stat rescans contain existing JSON/maps/directory/stat/atomic-writer allocations not bounded by the captured old segment count. They remain full-operation R1/library costs.
Observer/hooks are synchronous and borrowed; arbitrary callback allocations/reentrancy/error graphs have no demonstrated fixed total bound.

Owner.resizeLocked refuses growth after Close. Reservation must be pre-admitted before source Close and remain until original namespace phase disposal; reserved capacity is not already-open physical debt.

decision.implementation: Same original namespace scope reserves finite slots/name/census capacity before SourceClose. Post-close uses only reserved capacity; unsupported/out-of-bound/unavailable slots fail before open/mutation. Reuse requires actual quiescent successful Close. Uncertainty remains on same scope and failed operands.
prohibited: keeping source physical producer alive for bookkeeping
zeroing original DATA/R1/library or directory costs
